A shift from nonpassenger automobiles of 6,000 pounds and less GVWR to nonpassenger automobiles above 6,000 pounds GVWR might occur, for example, if the effect of a manufacturer's efforts to comply with an AFES for nonpassenger automobiles of 6,000 pounds or less GVWR were to reduce their performance significantly below that of the nonpassenger automobiles above 6,000 pounds GVWR or to reduce significantly the retail price differential between these two groups of automobiles. Such a shift would reduce the increase in the average fuel economy of the combined nonpassenger automobile fleet. If the shift were sufficiently large, there could be a net decline in the fleet average fuel economy.
•
In addition to the shift to nonpassenger automobiles above 6,000 pounds GVWR caused by consumer preference described above, the agency is concerned about a shift of automobiles out of the nonpassenger automobile of 6,000 pounds and less GVWR category that would result from manufacturers' changing the GVWR of these nonpassenger automobiles to a GVWR in excess of 6,000 pounds.
